hypothesis: With stock v11 TimeSeries, SAMPLES retention does not automatically retire original TAGS/TimeRanges metadata; old labels can inflate native PromQL metadata reads long after old physical sample partitions disappear.

binary.source_proof: StorageTimeSeries.cpp ## Retention explicitly states TAGS has no TTL by default even after all samples deleted; tags_deduplication_cache_expiration_seconds is not storage TTL.

fixture.native_query: avg by(project)(avg_over_time(tslab_r19_retention[1d])) and version with {project="p0"}; fixed result at 2026-10-20T12:05:00Z

method: Same runner and binary: create clean and aged v11 RAW UUID TimeSeries tables, each with exactly the same active 2000 series; aged has 48000 old series. Explicitly DROP aged SAMPLES partition ID 202608, not TTL daemon. Verify same active SAMPLES physical bytes/rows and exact native PromQL output. Before ABBA optimize both sources to one part per inner target, then stop merges. Two query selectors x four clean/aged/aged/clean phases, 3 warmups and 10 timed requests per phase; QueryFinish cpu/read_rows/read_bytes/SelectedMarks/memory p50; control drift bound 25%, no query result cache. Total 104 native queries.
math_bound: One 3h-lived node metric at 400 steady slots yields 3200 distinct IDs/day; 365d metadata 1.168m versus 15d samples 48000, ~24.33x metadata to live series. Synthetic aged case is 50k/2k=25x ID ratio. Observed 17x QueryFinish rows and 17.4x read bytes, not a theoretical necessity for all label selectivities/indices.
limitations: The experiment DROP PARTITION manually, modeling SAMPLES removal. It does not observe actual TTL scheduling, long-running ingest or cache expiry.
Only 50k single-sample IDs and one metric with four projects; no 1.33m 15d production-like distribution, privacy labels or external access controls.
Single runner ABBA; 15-17% broad control wall/CPU drift; latency effect must replicate independently.
All three inner targets are physically stable and merges explicitly stopped during timing; background behavior and concurrent readers/writes not tested.
A safe pruning strategy for TAGS requires late-arrival/resurrection, consistent TimeRanges, ID generator and ACL semantics; no automatic DELETE recommended.

next_action.step: Replicate same physical old-month drop on two independent runners with same fixture, source, binary and native query; require identical 17x metadata read inflation and full parity. Then test actual TTL expiration and safe metadata retention policy only after semantic proof for resumed/late series.
next_action.stop_condition: If any binary/fixture mismatch, actual retained IDs differ, SAMPLES data change or A/A CPU/wall drift >25%, mark invalid and preserve evidence; do not promote a cleanup patch.
